blueprint_concepts: Position of point wrt a circle

concept_use.Intercepts of a circle: Intercept lengths 2 sqrt(g^2 - c) = 6 and 2 sqrt(f^2 - c) = 8 give the equations for g, f and c.
concept_use.Position of point wrt a circle: The origin is inside exactly when S(0,0) = c < 0, which selects the two circles with c = -8.

solution: $g=-1$: $c=-8$, $f^{2}=8$ (two circles); $g=-7$: $c=40$, $f^{2}=56$ (two circles). So there are four circles
Origin inside $\iff S(0,0)=c<0$, true only for $c=-8$
solution_full: On the $x$-axis ($y=0$): $x^{2}+2gx+c=0$; the chord length is $|x_{1}-x_{2}|=2\sqrt{g^{2}-c}$. So $2\sqrt{g^{2}-c}=6$, i.e. $g^{2}-c=9$.
On the $y$-axis ($x=0$): $y^{2}+2fy+c=0$; the chord length is $2\sqrt{f^{2}-c}=8$, i.e. $f^{2}-c=16$.
$g=-7$: $c=40$ and $f^{2}=56$, so $f=\pm2\sqrt{14}$: two circles. In each case the radius squared $g^{2}+f^{2}-c$ is positive ($1$ and $65$), so all four circles are real.
The origin lies inside a circle exactly when $S(0,0)<0$, and $S(0,0)=c$.
For $g=-1$, $c=-8<0$: origin inside. For $g=-7$, $c=40>0$: origin outside.
Hence exactly $2$ circles contain the origin.
originality_note: New: the circle is fixed only up to two branches by a point and two intercept lengths (way 3, an object fixed by two conditions), and the count is filtered by the position of the origin read off from c. Closest known: circle through the origin cutting given intercepts. Different because: the circle does not pass through the origin, there are four circles and the position test separates them.

key_step: Solve the three equations from the two intercepts and the point, then use S(0,0) = c to test the origin.
justification: A chain of standard formulas (intercepts, point on circle, position by sign of S) with a two-way case split; no insight needed. Matches the routine multi-step L2 anchors such as 2026-P1-Q2 (L2).
